summary: Configured `inventory-worker` on node1 as an enabled, long-running systemd service. It writes persistent status data only under `/var/lib/inventory`, runs as a dynamic unprivileged user with no capabilities, and has `NoNewPrivileges` enforced. Persistence and recovery were verified after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Configured `/var/lib/inventory` as the service's only writable state directory
Made the remaining filesystem read-only, including temporary shared locations
Enabled `NoNewPrivileges`, removed all capabilities, and applied additional systemd hardening
Verified the live service namespace blocks writes outside `/var/lib/inventory`
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed a changed boot identity
Verified the service restarted automatically and retained then continued updating its data

evidence.summary: Shows the service enabled and active before and after restart, with a live PID, zero restart failures, and continuously updated worker data.

Runtime tests as the service UID blocked writes to `/etc`, `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/run`, `/dev/shm`, `/home`, and `/root`, while permitting `/var/lib/inventory`. Final configuration records the read-only hierarchy and sole writable path.
Live process evidence shows `NoNewPrivs: 1` and empty inherited, permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capability sets before and after restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID `55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358`; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID `35de64a9-bb63-4f56-95d8-dc07c285c02a`; the system and service were healthy, prior data remained present, and new records were appended.
